items.title: AI-capex faith is breaking, not the AI economy
items.detail: SOXX -4.5% on Jul 16 and TSMC's +77% y/y profit beat still could not hold the ADR. Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft are on track for as much as $725B of capex this year, and investors are now punishing the spenders while the chipmakers de-rate too. JPMorgan calls the divergence 'somewhat unsustainable'. This is the single largest factor in the index.

items.title: Gulf war escalation and the Strait of Hormuz
items.detail: Kuwait says Iran struck a power and desalination plant; US Central Command has completed six consecutive nights of strikes; Iran hit US bases in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and Syria. Hormuz crossings fell ~52% week-on-week per Kpler. Brent +4.6% to $88.10 and +14% on the week. A closure would be a genuine supply shock, and the interim peace deal now looks fragile.

items.title: S&P 500 closed below its 200-day moving average
items.detail: 7,457.69 versus a 200-day of 7,472.59 — the first close below it since Apr 8, and the index also lost its 50-day. One close is not a trend, but it removes the technical support that has underpinned every dip since spring.

items.title: Volatility is waking up
items.detail: VIX 18.03, up roughly 20% over the week. Still below the 20 'fear' threshold and well below the 25 that would flag a real regime change, but the speed of the move says complacency is evaporating.

items.title: Oil is now an inflation input again
items.detail: Brent at $88.10 with record refining margins feeds straight into headline CPI. That matters into the Jul 28-29 FOMC, where the Fed is expected to hold at 3.50-3.75%. An energy-led inflation print would take rate cuts off the table.

items.title: Yield curve is positively sloped
items.detail: 10Y 4.55% versus 2Y 4.18%, a +0.37 spread. No inversion signal, and the Fed is on hold rather than hiking. Rates are not the problem right now.

items.title: Leadership has narrowed to energy
items.detail: XLE +1.42% was the leading sector on Jul 17 while everything AI-adjacent fell. Narrow, commodity-driven leadership is less durable than broad participation, and it reverses instantly on a ceasefire headline.
